task_instance: Given a sample user request ('internal tool where employees upload PDF policy documents and anyone on the team can ask natural-language questions and get answers pulled from those documents, plus a nightly re-index job, no servers to manage'), use the skill's need-to-product map to actively surface the right Cloudflare products, explain why each fits and why alternatives don't, check current product behavior via web search, and produce a written architecture recommendation.
evidence: Read the skill's SKILL.md need-to-product table. Wrote a sample user_request.md describing the app. Attempted WebFetch on developers.cloudflare.com (blocked by the sandbox's egress proxy: EGRESS_BLOCKED), then used WebSearch instead, which succeeded and confirmed current AI Search (formerly AutoRAG) behavior: it reads from an R2 data source and continuously re-indexes new objects, which changed the recommendation (a hand-built nightly Queues/Workflows job is unnecessary; AI Search's built-in sync covers the 'nightly re-index' requirement). Wrote recommendation.md at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/cloudflare__skills__cloudflare@office-assistant/recommendation.md, which: (1) maps each stated need to a specific product (Workers, R2, AI Search, D1, Access) with a one-line justification tied to the skill's table, (2) explicitly explains why deferred/rejected options (Vectorize+Workers AI, Queues/Workflows, Pages, Containers) don't fit this specific request, (3) states a minimal recommended combination, and (4) lists the sources consulted (the skill doc plus the three URLs returned by web search). Verified the deliverable by re-reading its content in-context: it directly answers the sample request with a coherent, non-generic product combination and correct reasoning per the skill's stated method ('recommend a small, coherent combination', 'explain the deciding requirement', 'check current availability... before promising a fit'). The skill's core deliverable -- product discovery/recommendation text, not code or a running system -- was fully producible with only text file writes and web search/fetch; no code execution, binaries, or MCP/connector tools were needed or used.
notes: Direct WebFetch to developers.cloudflare.com was blocked by the sandbox's network egress proxy (not a runtime-capability blocker per the office-assistant grant, which allows 'fetch public web pages and search the public web'); WebSearch was used instead and was sufficient to get equivalent, current information, so this did not block the task.
